title: fleet-guards: CYCLE_MIN form pattern is locale-dependent - Unicode digits bypass magnitude guard
description: Edge-cases codereview of c5s6 fix (kimi-k3, pass 3) on scripts/fleet-guards.sh:11. The [!0-9] bracket range is collation-dependent: under glibc UTF-8 locales (verified LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 on this host) it folds multibyte digits, so Arabic-Indic '١٢٣', fullwidth '１４４０', Devanagari '१२' pass the case filter. Length check (line 17) passes (<=4 chars), then [ "$CYCLE_MIN" -gt 1440 ] errors rc 2 = condition false -> magnitude guard silently bypassed, exactly the mechanism lines 15-16 document but on the content dimension not length. Script then runs one full guard cycle (bd writes + metered credits API) and dies at line 148 with 'syntax error: operand expected' in $((CYCLE_MIN * 60)). Fail-crash, not hot loop, but under watchdog restart each restart burns one unthrottled cycle and guards die again (the overnight-blindness class the script exists to prevent). Verified fix, non-regressing: replace range with explicit list [!0123456789] (or scope LC_ALL=C to the validation). Fix both the guard line and the rejection tests.
close_reason: Fixed: fleet-guards.sh:11 form pattern [!0-9] replaced with explicit membership list [!0123456789] (collation-independent under every locale and both globasciiranges states) + comment documenting why ranges are unsafe (048n) alongside the existing c5s6 note. New committed rejection tests scripts/test_fleet_guards_cycle_min.py: 19 bad forms x 2 environments (default startup + BASH_ENV stub forcing globasciiranges off, which reproduces the 048n environment) — all reject rc=1 with usage error on stderr; defect mechanism reproduced on this host in isolation (old range PASSes ١٢٣ with shopt off; explicit list rejects). Acceptance 1/10/1440 verified entering the loop under both states manually (not committed — live loop has real bd/API side effects). bash -n clean; pytest 3/3 in 0.2s, fully offline. Note: defect does not fire on THIS host by default (bash 5.2.21 defaults globasciiranges on, which ASCII-bounds ranges) but fires on the worker6 host config the bead verified — the explicit list is safe in both. 3x codereview delegated to kimi-k3 per protocol: correctness PASS; security 2 findings; edge 2 findings — all 4 filed as new beads (xa9w P3 vacuous-locale reproduction, 2c6n P3 timeout-context + side-effect window, p6vc P4 tautological acceptance test, t082 P4 host-BASH_ENV leak) with dedup search performed (no pre-existing coverage).
